questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=t+2.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(t+2)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+4t+4)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+2{t}^{2}+4t)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+2+4 \\  & =\frac{19}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{19}{3}}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Polynomials
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(-2)y(-2)+x(0)y(0)+x(2)y(2).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=3-t+{t}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=3-t+{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(-2)=9,\,p(0)=3,\,p(2)=5.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(-2)p(-2)+p(0)p(0)+p(2)p(2)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(-2)]^{2}+[p(0)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(9)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(5)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{81+9+25} \\  & =\sqrt{115}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[\pi ,2\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[\pi ,2\pi ],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,(4{cos}^{2}⁡t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }((2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(3+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(3t+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t){|}_{\pi }^{2\pi } \\  & =(6\pi +0+0)-(3\pi +0+0) \\  & =3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identity 

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡t=\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector in an Inner Product Space
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)=2-3t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{(2-3t)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,(4-12t+9{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(4t-6{t}^{2}+3{t}^{3})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4-6+3 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
‖f(t)‖=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}}=1.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $‖f(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2-3t}{1} \\  & =2-3t\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector in an Inner Product Space
questions.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+5{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 

Normalize the  vector  $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨v,v⟩ & =(-1)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2+5\cdot (1\cdot 1) \\  & =1+4+5 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $v$, we divide $v$ by its norm $‖v‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{v}{‖v‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
